name: WebLLM
notable_features: Inference runs entirely inside the browser with no server component at all - the README's framing is 'Everything runs inside the browser with no server support and is accelerated with WebGPU'
OpenAI-API-compatible interface, so a WebLLM client is a drop-in for an OpenAI client in application code
Ships as the @mlc-ai/web-llm npm package with a documented web app build path; chat.webllm.ai is the live demo
Companion to MLC-LLM: the compilation toolchain that turns HF weights into the WebGPU-runnable artefact is MLC-LLM, not WebLLM. Understanding this split is the point (see [[mlc-llm]])
Version line v0.2.x after three years, which is a signal about the shape of the project: small, active, browser-scoped
Shares design DNA with the 2024 system paper, which frames browser inference as bandwidth-bound on consumer GPUs
hardware_caveats: The backend is WebGPU. There is no CUDA, no ROCm, no Metal path, no TPU, no Vulkan. 'Runs on your laptop' here means 'runs in your GPU-process sandbox via WebGPU', and hardware support is bounded by whatever your browser and OS expose - Safari and Firefox support has lagged Chrome's, and that is a browser limitation no one here can fix
Weights are MLC-compiled artefacts, not safetensors or GGUF. You need an MLC-LLM compile step; a HuggingFace safetensors checkpoint will not load directly
The device's browser is the sandbox: storage quotas, cross-origin isolation requirements and tab eviction all apply. This is not a server you can reason about with normal ops tooling
Model size is bounded by available VRAM/shared memory in the browser process, which on many laptops means single-digit-billion-parameter models at low bit width
v0.2.x after three years and 439 open issues; last push 2026-10-03 and v0.2.85 on 2026-09-08, so it is maintained, but the version scheme has never stabilised and there is no LTS line
No server-side scaling story whatsoever: no tensor parallelism, no multi-node, no request queue. One user, one tab
best_for: Client-side inference where the data must not leave the device - the actual reason this exists and the one thing nothing else does
Zero-ops prototypes and demos: no API key, no server, no cost, works offline after first load
Learning the WebGPU compute path for LLM inference, which is the cheapest available explanation of why decode is memory-bandwidth-bound
A privacy architecture reference for anyone designing on-device features into a web product
avoid_for: Anything multi-user - there is no server, so there is no concurrency story
Throughput or SLA work; browser inference is a UX feature, not a serving tier
Non-Chrome-first browsers, or any environment where WebGPU is unavailable or disabled
Consumers who need GGUF or HF safetensors - the artefact is MLC-compiled
notes: Relationship to [[mlc-llm]] stated precisely: MLC-LLM is the compiler and native/server runtime in the MLC stack; WebLLM is the browser-specific runtime that consumes MLC-LLM's compiled artefacts. Recording them separately is correct because their backends, deployment models and failure modes have nothing in common.
